title: The Broken Semester
premise: Ulyana Dravenmoor, a trans boy and star debater at Hollow Creek High, has spent three years carefully invisible while his family fractures over his identity. When the senior class essay prompt—'What would you save?'—goes viral, his anonymous answer about the town's dying Founders' Festival exposes him to the whole school. To win the scholarship that means escape, he must publicly champion the festival's revival, forcing him to debate in the open for the first time as himself. In the end, Ulyana loses the competition but wins something bigger: his family hears his argument at last, and the festival he saved becomes the stage where he is finally seen.
about_author: Casper Brightwater is the pen name of a former high-school debate coach who grew up in a small river town where one festival held everything together. They write stories about kids who learn that being heard is worth the risk of being seen.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet seventeen-year-old Ulyana mid-debate victory, then watch him shrink the moment he gets home, where his mother still uses his deadname and his father pretends not to notice anything. He catalogs his rules for invisibility. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of carefulness.

chapters.title: One Honest Question
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns the senior essay prompt 'What would you save?' Ulyana writes three safe drafts, then at 2 a.m. writes a fourth about the Founders' Festival—the one place he felt real before he learned to hide. Emotional beat: reckless honesty on paper.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Best friend Priya's POV. The essays are read aloud anonymously in class; someone records Ulyana's and posts it online. By lunch it has spread through Hollow Creek, though no one knows it's his. Priya recognizes every word. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in pride.

chapters.title: Deadname at Dinner
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A classmate quotes the essay at dinner within earshot of Ulyana's mother, who suspects but says nothing; his father defends the essay's 'whoever wrote it.' Ulyana lies badly. Emotional beat: the house's silence getting louder.

chapters.title: Festival of Ash
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The girls visit the shuttered festival grounds, closed since budget cuts three years ago. Priya reveals her own stake: her grandmother was the last Festival Queen. They find the old debate trophy case—Ulyana's name from before. Emotional beat: grief for what towns and people lose when they stop celebrating themselves.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Debater
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At school, rival Theo Vance argues the festival is a waste of money, echoing the school board. Ulyana dismantles him from the back of the room without claiming authorship. Ms. Okafor watches him too closely. Emotional beat: the thrill of arguing as himself, anonymously.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, board president's son, needs a signature issue for his mayoral-intern ambitions and proposes a public debate: should Hollow Creek revive the Founders' Festival? The essay's author is invited to respond. Ulyana must decide whether to claim it. Emotional beat: ambition sharpening into a trap.

chapters.title: Claiming It
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With Priya's hand on his shoulder, Ulyana signs up under his chosen name in front of the whole cafeteria. The whisper travels faster than he does. His mother sees the signup sheet when she drops off his forgotten lunch. Emotional beat: terror and vertigo of visibility.

chapters.title: The Quiet War at Home
chapters.summary: Mother's POV (Dana). Dana confronts her own history—her brother who left town and was never mentioned again—and realizes she's repeating her parents' silence. She reads the essay twice and cries into the good dishes. Emotional beat: love trapped behind fear.

chapters.title: Debate Camp for One
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya and Ulyana prep in the library, sparring every anti-festival argument. Ulyana admits he's never debated anything that mattered to him. Ms. Okafor offers coaching and a warning: the board will make it personal. Emotional beat: found family forming around a folding table.

chapters.title: Personal Attacks
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Theo's op-ed outs Ulyana's deadname and calls the essay 'a confused child's fantasy,' framing the festival fight as a fight about 'tradition.' The hallway becomes hostile. Ulyana almost withdraws. Emotional beat: the specific cruelty of having your past weaponized.

chapters.title: What Tradition Means
chapters.summary: Grandmother Irena's POV. Ulyana visits Priya's grandmother, who shows him festival photos—including one of Dana as a girl, crowned Junior Harvest Princess, beaming beside Irena's sister. Tradition, Irena says, is 'a story we keep choosing.' Emotional beat: reclamation of the word tradition.

chapters.title: The First Debate
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Town hall, packed. Ulyana opens shakily, then finds his footing arguing that the festival isn't nostalgia but infrastructure—for belonging. Theo counters with economics. It ends in a draw and a standing ovation Ulyana can barely hear over his own heartbeat. Emotional beat: first public breath as himself.

chapters.title: Father's Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Father's POV (Marcus). Marcus watches the debate replay, recognizing his son's cadence as his own father's. He remembers carrying five-year-old Ulyana on his shoulders at the last festival. He doesn't come upstairs—but he leaves the porch light on. Emotional beat: love expressed as small light.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Someone trashes the festival grounds storage shed, destroying costumes and the Queen's crown, and Theo's fingerprints are all over the timing—right before the deciding vote. But the evidence points instead to Theo's father. Emotional beat: fury and the discovery that the enemy is bigger than a rival.

chapters.title: The Board's Gambit
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The school board cancels the final debate, declaring the matter settled. Ulyana realizes the debate was never the point—silencing him was. Ms. Okafor risks her job by suggesting they take the argument somewhere the board can't gavel down. Emotional beat: righteous anger finding a channel.

chapters.title: The Essay Goes Loud
chapters.summary: Multiple short POVs. Students, teachers, and shop owners begin reading their own answers to 'What would you save?' at open mics, tagging the school. The movement outgrows Ulyana, which terrifies and frees him. Emotional beat: a single honest question becoming a chorus.

chapters.title: Concessions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds proof his father ordered the vandalism and faces a choice: bury it or burn his own future exposing it. Haunted by how Ulyana argued—with belief instead of strategy—Theo testifies before the county. Emotional beat: a rival choosing integrity over inheritance.

chapters.title: The Last Debate
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. County chamber, final vote. Ulyana speaks last, abandoning his prepared case to tell the truth about hiding, the essay, and the festival where he first felt like himself. His mother stands up mid-speech—not to object, but to say 'his name is Ulyana.' Emotional beat: climax; the argument at home finally won by being lost gracefully.

chapters.title: Vote
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The council approves a one-year festival trial, funded partly by community pledges including, quietly, Theo's father's company. Ulyana learns he lost the scholarship essay contest to a freshman. He laughs until he cries. Emotional beat: deflation giving way to perspective.

chapters.title: Founders' Day, Restored
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The festival returns, imperfect and handmade. Ulyana debates Theo for fun on the bandstand, loses on purpose, wins the crowd. His father fixes the sound system; his mother hands out programs with his name printed correctly. Emotional beat: joy earned, not granted.

chapters.title: What I Would Save
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue-style. Ulyana submits his college essay—revised, signed, unhidden—about saving a festival and being saved by the people who helped him. He packs for a school that accepted the real him. Final line echoes the prompt. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won hope.
